jobs.occupation: Shape the Future of Digital Growth at NutraQ
jobs.description:
What if you could own the digital customer journey across an international eCommerce business, with the mandate to turn customer insight, technology and commercial opportunities into measurable growth?

 

NutraQ is creating a new Head of eCommerce role to lead the next stage of our international web platforms and digital customer experience. You will own the roadmap, lead our Web team (UX Designer, Web Analyst and Tech Lead) and drive improvements across conversion, customer journeys, analytics and digital revenue. You will work where commercial strategy, product and technology meet, together with commercial teams, Data & Analytics and IT. The role reports to the Head of IT.

 
What you will be responsible for:
• Own the eCommerce roadmap and backlog, turning customer insight, commercial opportunities and business needs into clear priorities.
• Lead and develop the Web team and relevant external partners, setting clear goals, priorities and ways of working.
• Drive digital growth across markets and concepts: traffic, conversion, revenue and long-term customer life time value.
• Build an experimentation culture using A/B testing, analytics and behavioural data.
• Optimise end-to-end customer journey, including UX/UI, landing pages, checkout, pricing, offers and subscription flows, with strong focus on upsell, retention and website performance.
• Work with the Tech Lead and commercial teams to prioritise initiatives with the highest impact and ROI,  and drive standardisation across markets and concepts.
• Explore opportunities in AI, automation and emerging eCommerce technology, while ensuring solutions are scalable and compliant with GDPR and consumer protection requirements. What you bring
We care more about what you have achieved than about your current title. You may be a Product Owner, Product Manager, eCommerce Manager, Digital Product Manager or similar.

• Strong experience in eCommerce and digital products, with measurable results in traffic and conversion, digital sales, and customer value.
• Experience owning and prioritising roadmaps and backlogs based on business value, using agile ways of working.
• Hands-on experience with CRO, A/B testing and experimentation.
• A strong interest in data, analytics and tracking, and a solid understanding of digital funnels, checkout flows and customer journeys.
• Technical understanding and curiosity to be a strong partner to the Tech Lead and development team.
• Strong stakeholder management and the ability to align commercial and technical teams.
• Leadership experience, or a track record of bringing different disciplines together.
• Excellent written and spoken English.
Experience from D2C, subscription models, international eCommerce or multi-brand environments is a strong advantage.

 
How you work
You are driven, proactive and create momentum. You combine sharp analytical thinking with commercial acumen. You lean on data insights in making decisions and you focus the team on what creates the most value. You are a hands-on leader who is comfortable challenging existing solutions and standing behind your recommendations, while building strong relationships across business and technology. As a leader, you are ambitious and you create enthusiasm and a fun work environment. You have a clear vision and point direction with trust and support, and you enjoy developing your people.

 

You are a cultural ambassador who likes to come to the office, and identify with our core values: Responsible, Respectful, Brave and Innovative.

 
Your opportunity to make an impact
Because the role is new, you will shape both what NutraQ prioritises and how the Tech Lead and developers will deliver on commercial needs, growth and shape the future of our web platform and architecture. Your first focus will be to improve how priorities are set across markets, make experimentation and CRO more systematic, and build a clear, data-driven roadmap. You will see your success directly in traffic, conversion, customer life time value, retention and delivery performance.

 
What we offer
• A newly created leadership role with real influence on an international, subscription-based digital business.
• Ownership of web platforms serving multiple brands, concepts and markets.
• The chance to shape how NutraQ works with data, experimentation and AI.
• A professional, collaborative and diverse culture where people know how to have fun.
• 
Competetive benefits, and modern offices at Skøyen in Oslo. Being present and part of the team there is an important part of the role.

 

If this sounds like your next step, we look forward to receiving your application.

See what our employees say about NutraQ

 

Please contact Emelie Isosalo Jansson (+47 94 83 42 26 / eij@greatpeople.no) or Sarah Schrøder (+47 950 02 244/ scs@greatpeople.no) for a conversation about this opportunity.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

NutraQ Group is an international health and beauty company owned by Orkla. We develop, produce and sell products directly to consumers through a digital subscription model. NutraQ has more than 230 employees and operates in 15 European markets and the US.

 

Our culture is our competitive advantage, and we are ranked among the top-tier companies in Great Place To Work. Our ambition is to have the best subscription-based platform in Europe.

jobs.occupation: Want to make a global sports platform with 4 million users truly data driven? Spond is hiring a Data Analyst (apply without a CV or cover letter)

As Data Analyst in the Data & Insight team, you turn all that activity into insight Spond can act on. The team is fairly new, with a head of data, a data engineer and another analyst, and you get a real say in which standards you set, how you build data products and how you use AI to work faster. The stack is Databricks, dbt, Omni and Mixpanel.

Turning open questions from the product teams and other parts of Spond into analyses that change decisions

Building analyses, self service tools and data models that colleagues use every day

Bringing in new data sources and modelling them in dbt

Helping colleagues across Spond find answers in the data themselves through training and self service

• 

Have a few years of experience as a data analyst or similar, ideally from a software company, a startup or a tech consultancy

• 

Write advanced SQL on your own and have experience with Databricks or Snowflake and dbt

• 

Have used product analytics tools such as Mixpanel or Amplitude

• 

Can go deep in the data and still explain the bigger picture to non technical colleagues

• 

Are pragmatic and structured, take ownership and enjoy working with colleagues at the office

• 

Speak fluent English. Python and Norwegian are a plus

We offer

• 

A key role in a new team with a clear mandate to make Spond data driven, with AI and data at the centre

• 

A product that makes everyday life easier for millions of players, coaches and parents

• 

Competitive salary, a personal learning budget, insurance, pension and healthcare

• 

Flexible hours, home office options and access to company cabins for you and your family

• 

Newly renovated offices in Kvadraturen in Oslo with a café and a private gym

jobs.description:
The International School of Bergen is seeking an experienced, compassionate, and highly skilled School Counsellor to join our vibrant IB World School in Norway.

Hva vi ser etter

Application

We welcome applications from suitably qualified and experienced counsellors who are genuinely committed to relocating to Norway and becoming part of our school community.

Please submit the following documents by email with the subject line "US School Counsellor Application" to laura.mcguffie@isbergen.no:

• 

A current CV.

• 

A covering letter explaining your relevant counseling experience, qualifications, experience working with children and young people, and motivation for working at the International School of Bergen.

• 

Contact details for two professional referees, including your current or most recent employer.

Important - Relocation to Norway

Please only apply if you are seriously considering relocating to Bergen, Norway.

Candidates who are currently living outside Norway should be prepared to relocate and meet the relevant Norwegian immigration, visa and work permit requirements, where applicable.

As part of the application process, candidates may be asked to provide information regarding their nationality/passport country and current country of residence so that the school can establish the appropriate immigration and work permit requirements.

This is an on-site based position in Bergen, Norway.

Safeguarding

The International School of Bergen is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people.

All appointments must provide a police background check from your home country and any country you have resided in for 6+ months in the last 10 years. Police background checks must be no more than 3 months old and can be presented prior to appointment.

All staff are expected to uphold the school's safeguarding policies and Code of Conduct.

Previous applicants should reapply if you are still seriously interested in the position.

If you have any questions in regards to this position, please contact Peter Ledger, Director peter.ledger@isbergen.no or Laura McGuffie, HR and Finance Manager laura.mcguffie@isbergen.no

Applications will be reviewed as they are received. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if a suitable candidate is identified, so early applications are encouraged.

Closing Date for applications is 27th November 2026

Arbeidsoppgaver

The role includes:

•

• 

Promoting resilience, self-management, positive relationships and emotional wellbeing.

• 

Working collaboratively with teachers to identify and support students requiring additional care.

• 

Advising school leadership on student wellbeing, safeguarding and pastoral care.

• 

Liaising effectively with parents and guardians to support student success.

• 

Coordinating referrals to external professionals and Norwegian support services where appropriate.

• 

Supporting crisis response and student reintegration following significant life events.

• 

Maintaining accurate, confidential records in accordance with GDPR and Norwegian legislation.

• 

Contributing to safeguarding procedures and child protection practices.

• 

Supporting transitions between PYP and MYP where applicable), ensuring continuity of care.

• 

Promoting inclusion, diversity, intercultural understanding and student voice.

The Successful Candidate Will Have

Essential

• 

A recognised qualification in Counselling, School Psychology, Educational Psychology, Social Work or a related field.

• 

Professional registration or eligibility for registration where applicable.

• 

Experience working with children and adolescents in a school setting.

• 

Strong understanding of child and adolescent development.

• 

Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.

• 

Demonstrated ability to build trusting relationships with students, families and staff.

• 

Commitment to safeguarding and child protection.

• 

High levels of professionalism, integrity and confidentiality.

• 

Excellent spoken and written English.

• 

A genuine willingness and ability to relocate to Bergen, Norway.

Desirable

• 

Previous experience within an IB World School.

• 

Knowledge of the IB Learner Profile and IB Approaches to Learning (ATL).

• 

Experience supporting internationally mobile or multilingual students.

• 

Experience working within multicultural communities.

• 

Knowledge of trauma-informed and restorative practices.

Personal Attributes

We are looking for someone who is:

• 

Compassionate and approachable.

• 

Calm and solution-focused.

• 

Collaborative and reflective.

• 

Culturally responsive and internationally minded.

• 

An excellent listener with sound professional judgement.

• 

Passionate about student wellbeing and inclusion.

• 

Committed to continuous professional learning.

• 

Open to embracing life and work within an international school community in Norway.

Vi tilbyr

Why Join Us?

Our school offers:

• 

A welcoming and diverse international community.

• 

Students representing many nationalities and cultures.

• 

A collaborative and supportive staff culture.

• 

Commitment to ongoing professional development.

• 

Competitive salary and pension.

• 

The opportunity to live and work in one of the world's most beautiful and family-friendly countries.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

About Our School

ISB is a co-educational private day school which is authorised to deliver the International Baccalaureate PYP and MYP programmes. The school currently has approximately 250 students enrolled from more than 30 nations and is experiencing expanding enrolment. Classes are small with a maximum of 20 students in each instructional group.

Our school is committed to developing internationally minded young people who embody the attributes of the IB Learner Profile. We believe that student wellbeing is fundamental to learning, and we are looking for a counsellor who shares our commitment to nurturing the academic, social, emotional and personal development of every learner.

Working collaboratively with students, families, teachers and school leaders, the successful candidate will play a central role in promoting wellbeing, inclusion, safeguarding and positive mental health across the school community.

jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate in Novel Object Representations for Cultural Heritage (CH) Objects
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
Are you interested in pursuing a doctoral degree in an international research environment? This position offers the opportunity to join the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network UNCHANGE, collaborate with academic, museums, and industry partners across Europe, and develop expertise within a multidisciplinary research project on cultural heritage science.

As part of the UNCHANGE network, the PhD Candidate will participate in workshops, conferences, transferable skills training, and research secondments with partner organisations. The position provides opportunities for both academic and professional development within an international setting.

The successful candidate will be offered a fixed-term, full-time position as a PhD Candidate for a period of 36 months and will be enrolled in a PhD programme leading to the award of a doctoral degree. The expected start date is 1 August 2027, and the Head of unit will be the immediate supervisor for employment-related matters.
About the project
About the UNCHANGE project  

UNCHANGE (UNderstanding change in Cultural HeritAge: the Next Generation of Experts) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network that brings together leading European universities, research institutions, and industry partners to train the next generation of heritage scientists. The project focuses on understanding, documenting, and monitoring change in cultural heritage using advanced technologies, including imaging, materials analysis, artificial intelligence, and data science. Through an interdisciplinary and international research environment, UNCHANGE equips doctoral candidates with the skills needed to address current and future challenges in cultural heritage conservation and preservation.

About the specific Doctoral projectObjectives: (1) Investigate novel object representations, such as Gaussians and Ray Fields, in measuring change for CH objects. (2) Investigate novel object representations in capturing and visualizing CH objects. The above objectives reflect current trends in the development of new object representations that are ‘AI-Friendly’, given the pervasiveness of AI methods in all types of processing.Expected results: Determination of the effect of machine learning-friendly object representations in capturing, visualizing and measuring change on CH objects.
Duties of the position
• Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate.
• Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above.
• Academic publications and popular science dissemination.
• Participate in the Visual Computing research group.
• Participate in the network’s joint research and training activities, both online and in person across the UNCHANGE partner institutions and contribute to UNCHANGE project deliverables in accordance with the Description of Action and the project's governance procedures.
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions. Particularly, secondments of a few months’ duration are foreseen to NTNU Museum (Trondheim) and Peggy Guggenheim Collection, Venezia.
Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must have a relevant master's degree in computer science, imaging science or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis.
• You must have experience in Visual Computing, Machine Learning, excellent programming skills and a desire to apply your skills to Cultural Heritage.
• At the date of recruitment, you must NOT have been awarded a doctoral degree. Researchers who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis but have not yet formally been awarded the degree are also not eligible.
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme in computer science, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
• Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position.
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your master’s degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
• Excellent oral and written communication skills in English.
• You must comply with the MSCA mobility rule: you must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of the recruiting organisation for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before recruitment (short stays such as holidays are not taken into account). 
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• Good oral and written presentation skills in Norwegian or one of the languages of the consortium partners (in addition to English).Personal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: 

• Work independently
• Work in a structured way, set goals and make plans to achieve them
• Show curiosity and a strong motivation for the subject
• Analyze data, assess different perspectives and draw well-founded conclusions 
• Be flexible and open to adjusting the plan for the project as needed 
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
 

• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)
• Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2)
• As an employee in Norway, the successful candidate will normally be a member of the Norwegian National Insurance Scheme, which provides access to public healthcare and social security benefits in accordance with applicable legislation and regulations.
•  
As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. This will cover the MSCA Living Allowance. In addition, mobility allowance and family allowance may be provided in accordance with MSCA regulations.

A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary.

The employment period is 3 years.

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Computer Science within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment.

The position is conditional on external funding.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The successful applicant must devote full working time to the project and the doctoral training programme.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to be in conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.
About the application
The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in Norwegian/a Scandinavian language or English.

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

The application must include: 

• Transcripts and diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degrees
• Curriculum Vitae 
• Copy of master’s thesis. If you have recently submitted your master’s thesis, you can attach a draft of the thesis. Documentation of a completed master’s degree must be presented before taking up the position.
• Project outline, as you imagine it (maximum 1500 words/4 pages) 
• English language certificates
• Names and contact information of three relevant referees
If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).

jobs.description:
About the position
NHH's Department of Finance is seeking to add faculty members with an internationally competitive research agenda. Candidates should have a strong research record or potential, as demonstrated by existing working papers, and ideally by publications in top-tier finance journals. The school primarily seeks applicants with a degree from an internationally recognised high-quality institution. Applicants should have completed, or be close to completing, a PhD in finance or a related field. We are interested in candidates within all areas of finance.

The position will involve a competitive teaching load, which also includes some graduate student supervision and administrative duties. Faculty members at NHH are expected to be good teachers. NHH offers the opportunity to participate in a program for university pedagogy, and candidates hired for tenure-track position as Assistant Professor or four-year position as Assistant Professor must take one basic module of the program during the fixed-term period. Candidates hired for the tenure-track position as Associate Professor, who cannot document at least 200 hours of pedagogical coursework at the time of promotion to a permanent position, must complete this program within two years.
 
NHH values effective communication and expects our faculty to have good language skills in both English and Norwegian. Candidates hired for a tenure-track position are required to master proficiency in Norwegian at the B2 level (The Common European Framework) within three years of appointment to a permanent position. Candidates hired for a tenure-track position as Associate Professor are required to master proficiency in Norwegian at the B2 level within three years of appointment to the tenure-track position. Swedish and Danish are considered equivalent to Norwegian. NHH offers courses in Norwegian for employees who may not initially have Norwegian or another Scandinavian language proficiency.
NHH offers
We offer a seven-year tenure-track position, either as Assistant Professor or Associate Professor, depending on qualifications. As a successful tenure-track Associate Professor, NHH will grant a full professorship, all dependent on specific criteria. We also offer a four-year Assistant Professor position. Four-year Assistant Professor of Finance position will only be relevant for successful applicants who cannot be hired in a tenure-track position due to the regulations related to such positions. To be qualified for a tenure-track position, it should not be more than five years since the PhD degree was achieved (may be extended, for example in connection with statutory leaves). For candidates undertaking their PhD, the expected completion of the PhD thesis should be no later than the date of commencement in the position.

Salary is negotiable according to Norwegian State Salary Scale. All state employees will be members of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK), and receive good welfare benefits such as paid parental leave. External research grants and teaching in executive programs offer opportunities for supplementing this salary.

Female associate professors appointed to permanent academic positions may apply for research leave (sabbatical) with half the standard accrual period, in accordance with NHH’s applicable guidelines. This will apply for the first two years of research leave.
General information
The appointee must comply with the guidelines that apply to the position at any time.

NHH emphasises diversity and encourages qualified candidates to apply for the position regardless of gender, age, disability and cultural background.

In the assessment of applicants, international experience and qualifications will be emphasised. For the sake of gender balance at NHH, female applicants will be given preference in the event of equivalent qualifications among candidates.

The application should contain details of the applicant's scientific and pedagogical education and work experience. Please include a cover letter, CV, list of publications, research statement, teaching evaluations, and any other documents that are useful in evaluating your application. In addition, the applicant should provide a teaching statement, which also includes an overview and assessment of the applicants' teaching experience. A maximum of 10 published or unpublished research papers (for the position as Associate Professor tenure-track) or a maximum of 5 published or unpublished research papers (for the position as Assistant Professor tenure-track or four-year Assistant Professor) should also be attached for evaluation. The application and enclosed documentation should be submitted through the Jobbnorge online portal. To open the application, please click 'Apply for this job'. For English version, go to the menu at the top right corner.
 
Three reference letters (in PDF) attesting to the candidate's research abilities should be submitted by the referees directly to NHH at hr-references@nhh.no, no later than 9 December 2026.

As part of the recruitment process, a background check may be conducted with the candidates' consent.

In accordance with §25 (2) of the Freedom of Information Act, information about applicants may be made public even if they have requested not to have their names entered on the list of applicants. Applicants will be notified if their request is not granted.

Enquiries may be directed to Recruiting Chair, Department of Finance, Tore Leite, e-mail: tore.leite@nhh.no

Deadline for applications is 9 December 2026. This date also applies to the submission of publications/written work.

jobs.occupation: PhD Position  - in the Oral Physiology and Cancer Research Group (OPCG)
jobs.description:
About the position 
A PhD research fellowship is available in the Oral Physiology and Cancer Research Group (OPCG) at the Institute of Oral biology, Faculty of Dentistry, the University of Oslo. One of our group’s major interests is the study of how extracellular vesicles from cancer cells affect various normal cells, both in the immediate vicinity of the tumor and at a distance, changing their phenotype to support the growing tumor mass. In the proposed project, we aim to investigate the effect of extracellular vesicles from oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) on the function of normal cells, including endothelial cells. 
 
The candidate will apply various experimental methods to assess whether the normal phenotype changes towards a tumor-supporting one upon OSCC-derived extracellular vesicle exposure. Such alterations may include increased proliferation, modifications of intracellular Ca2+ signalling pathways, shifts in the metabolic profile and more.     
More about the position
The main purpose of the fellowship is research training leading to the successful completion of a PhD degree. 

Project title: “Tumor-host interaction in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC)”

This is a 100% full-time, three-year PhD Research Fellowship position. The successful candidate is expected to produce three scientific papers and a doctoral thesis. The place of work is Oslo, Norway.
More about the fellowship
Admission to the PhD programme at the Faculty of Dentistry is a prerequisite for taking up the position. The candidate is expected to complete the project within the fellowship period. A final plan for the research training must be approved and formalised no later than three months after the start of the position.

The main supervisor will be Professor Trude Marie Haug - Institute of Oral Biology
Qualification requirements
Mandatory requirements

• Applicants must hold a Master’s degree equivalent to a Norwegian master’s degree in molecular biology, cell biology, dentistry or in another field relevant to the research project.
• The Master’s thesis must have a grade B or better in the Norwegian educational system.
• A good level of written and oral communication skills in English is required.
• English requirements for applicants from outside of EU/EEA countries and exemptions from the requirements: https://www.odont.uio.no/english/research/phd/regulations/supplementary-rules.html
• Publications in international peer-reviewed scientific journals will be advantageous but not required
Experience in the following methods will be advantageous:

• Cell culturing
• Standard molecular biological techniques and immunohistochemistry
• Analysis of -omics data
• Intracellular Ca2+ imagingPersonal skills:
• Ability to work independently and in an interdisciplinary scientific environment
• Self-motivation, creativity, genuine curiosity about the subject, work discipline, professional ethics, and ambition
• Strong practical and analytical skills
• Good social and collaboration skills
We need different perspectives in our work

• UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that aims to provide an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. We fulfil our mission most effectively when we draw on different experiences, backgrounds and perspectives.
• We will do our best to accommodate individual needs. Relevant adjustments may include adaptations to working hours, tasks, digital or physical tools, or other practical measures. Applicants with an immigrant background, a disability or gaps in their CV are encouraged to indicate this in the application portal. UiO invites at least one qualified applicant from each of these groups to interview in accordance with applicable state-sector procedures.Why should you choose us?
• A clearly defined and fully funded three-year PhD project with established core infrastructure.
• Dedicated supervision and research-training.
• An interdisciplinary and internationally connected research environment at the Faculty of Dentistry.
• A workplace with good development and career opportunities, good welfare schemes and up to 1.5 hours per week of exercise during working hours.(Good welfare schemes)
• Membership in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (Statens Pensjonskasse), with beneficial pension, mortgage and insurance arrangements.
• Oslo’s family-friendly environment, with extensive cultural and outdoor opportunities.
• Dedicated mentoring and a professionally stimulating working environment.
• Salary in position as Doctoral Research Fellow, position code 1017 in salary range NOK from 565000 - to 620 000, depending on competence and experience. From the salary, 2 percent is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension Fund.
Read more about the benefits of working in the public sector at Employer Portal.
How to apply
Your application must include:

• A cover letter of 1-2 pages describing your motivation for the position, your relevant academic and practical experience, and how your background matches the project.
• A CV summarizing education, work experience, research experience and other qualifying activities.
• Copies of diplomas, academic transcripts and certificates. Applicants should retrieve available results from Vitnemålsportalen; where this is not possible, copies must be uploaded.
• Documentation of English proficiency where required under the Faculty’s supplementary admission rules.
• A complete list of publications and other academic work, if applicable, together with the work the applicant wishes the evaluation committee to consider.
• A copy of your master thesis if possible.
• Contact information for two to three references, including name, position, relationship to the applicant, e-mail address and telephone number.
• The application and all attachments must be submitted through UiO’s electronic recruitment system, Jobbnorge, by clicking “Apply for the position”. All documentation must be in English or a Scandinavian language. Applicants with education from outside Scandinavia should include an explanation of their university’s grading system and a Diploma Supplement where available. A recognition statement from the Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), if already obtained, may also be attached.

The best-qualified candidates will be invited to interview and may be asked to give a brief presentation of previous research or technical work.General information

jobs.occupation: IT Service Desk Technician
jobs.description:
Location: Oslo, Norway
About the role
At Schibsted, reliable IT services are essential to helping our employees do their best work.

We are looking for an IT Service Desk Technician to join our Service Desk team in Oslo, providing high-quality technical support to employees across our organisation, primarily in Norway and Sweden.

Our Service Desk is more than a traditional first-line support function. We resolve approximately 80% of all incoming IT requests and incidents within the team, which means you will have the opportunity to work with a wide range of technical challenges, take ownership of issues and develop your troubleshooting skills.

You will work in an international environment where customer satisfaction, technical expertise and continuous improvement are key priorities. Our IT operations follow IT Service Management (ITSM) principles and ITIL practices, with a strong focus on efficient problem-solving, knowledge sharing and improving the employee IT experience.
Your responsibilities
As an IT Service Desk Technician, your main responsibilities will include:

• 
Deliver high-quality IT support: Provide professional, friendly and solution-oriented technical support to employees through phone, email and other support channels.

• 
Troubleshoot and resolve technical issues: Investigate and resolve incidents involving computers, operating systems, applications, user accounts, access and other workplace technologies.

• 
Own incidents and service requests: Register, prioritise, investigate, document and follow up on cases in our ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Halo), taking responsibility for driving issues towards resolution.

• 
Ensure a great user experience: Communicate clearly with users, provide regular updates and manage expectations throughout the support process.

• 
Drive efficient resolution and knowledge sharing: Contribute to our high resolution rate by developing technical knowledge, documenting solutions and supporting a shift-left approach.

• 
Collaborate and continuously improve: Work closely with colleagues and other IT teams to resolve complex issues and improve processes related to Incident, Problem, Change and Knowledge Management.

• 
Manage IT equipment and suppliers: Support ordering, inventory management and distribution of IT equipment and accessories, including coordination with external suppliers.
What we're looking for
We are looking for someone who enjoys solving technical challenges, takes ownership of problems and genuinely likes helping people.

You are curious about technology, comfortable investigating unfamiliar issues and motivated by finding solutions rather than simply passing problems on to someone else.

You enjoy working in an environment where priorities can change quickly and where teamwork, knowledge sharing and customer satisfaction are essential.
Skills and knowledge
To succeed in this role, we believe you have:

• 
A good understanding of computers, operating systems, software and common workplace IT technologies.

• 
The ability to troubleshoot technical issues in a structured and logical way.

• 
Familiarity with, or an interest in learning, technologies such as Windows, macOS, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace and Microsoft Entra ID.

• 
An understanding of the importance of documenting incidents, solutions and technical information.

• 
The ability to communicate technical information clearly to users with different levels of IT knowledge.

• 
Professional proficiency in Norwegian or Swedish, as well as English, both written and spoken.
Nice to have
The following qualifications are an advantage, but not essential:

• 
Previous experience working in an IT Service Desk, IT Support or similar technical support role.

• 
Around two years of relevant technical experience or education.

• 
Experience working with ITSM platforms such as ServiceNow or Halo.

• 
Knowledge of ITIL principles and IT Service Management processes.

• 
Relevant IT certifications or technical training.

• 
Experience with IT equipment management, inventory control or supplier coordination.

• 
Experience with AI tools and technologies, particularly using AI to improve IT support, automate tasks, enhance troubleshooting or streamline workflows.

We value practical skills, curiosity and a willingness to learn. You do not need to meet every preferred qualification to be considered for the role.
Who you are
We believe the following qualities will help you succeed:

• 
Customer oriented: You enjoy helping others, understand their needs and take pride in delivering excellent service.

• 
Problem-solving: You approach technical challenges with curiosity, persistence and a structured mindset, taking responsibility for finding solutions.

• 
Communication: You explain technical issues clearly, listen actively and keep users informed throughout the support process.

• 
Adaptable: You are comfortable handling changing priorities, learning new technologies and working in a dynamic IT environment.

• 
Collaborative: You enjoy sharing knowledge, supporting colleagues and contributing to a positive and supportive team environment.
Why join us?
You will join a Service Desk team in Oslo where technical problem-solving, collaboration and high-quality service go hand in hand.

Unlike traditional first-line support roles, our team handles and resolves the majority of incoming IT issues, giving you the opportunity to work with a broad range of technologies and technical challenges.

You will support colleagues across Norway and Sweden, work with modern workplace technologies and contribute to continuously improving how IT services are delivered.

We believe great IT support is about more than fixing technical problems. It is about taking ownership, building trust and making people's working lives easier.
